newsitem.title: INDIA: Driver's death raises India train crash toll to 13.
newsitem.headline: Driver's death raises India train crash toll to 13.

text.p: The death toll in Monday's train collision near the Indian capital rose to 13, doctors and police said on Tuesday.
"The driver of the Karnataka Express died today," said an official at the railway police station in Faridabad, on the outskirts of New Delhi.
Railway officials on Monday said the accident was caused by human error when the speeding Karnataka Express overshot a stop signal on a loop line and rammed into the slower-moving Himsagar Express.
Doctors at a hospital in this industrial town said three injured passengers were in serious condition. At least 82 people were injured in the collision.
Railway officials said rail services had largely resumed on Tuesday through Faridabad, an important junction.
A similar accident occurred in Faridabad in May when a passenger train overshot a stop signal and crashed into a freight train. No casualties were reported in that accident.

Monday's disaster was the latest to hit the accident-prone Indian railways. On Sunday one person died and 28 were injured when two coaches of a train were derailed in the northern state of Uttar Pradesh.
Latest government figures show 594 people died in 398 railway accidents in 1995/96 (April-March), compared with 305 deaths in 501 accidents the previous year.

India's railways cover a vast network spread over 62,915 km (39,321 miles) and in 1995/96 carried 123 million passengers on long-distance journeys. Trains are the cheapest mode of transport across the huge country.

In August 1995, at least 350 people were killed in India's worst train accident, which occurred near the town of Ferozabad, 200 km (125 miles) from New Delhi when two trains collided. The accident was blamed on human error.
